chunks: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

Verily, the children of the Muslims are designated at Allah, the Mighty and High, as intercessors and those who will receive intercession. When they reach twelve years of age, good deeds are written for them, and when they reach puberty, bad deeds are written against them.

key_terms.موسمون: Designated or marked with a specific attribute

ai.seo_question: At what age do Muslim children become accountable for their sins according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the transitional state of Muslim children, emphasizing their unique spiritual status as intercessors for their parents before the onset of individual accountability. It establishes a clear theological distinction between the age of twelve, where good deeds are recorded but sins are not yet counted, and the age of puberty (bulugh), which marks the beginning of full legal and moral responsibility (taklif) in Shia jurisprudence.
